Alice: Heads up — on the new HF->Redwood conversion for the gptj-variant we onboarded, tool-calling JSON blobs are getting corrupted at inference time. Seems related to special tokens + role markers.
Ben: Can you paste a minimal repro + model/tokenizer name?
Alice: Using hf_gptj-v1 (sentencepiece fallback). Repro: convert with our hf-converter, load in rw-runtime, run a tool call with a JSON-mode sentinel + <tool> tag and you get truncated JSON. Example snippet from the prompt:
```
system: <<SYS>>
user: call_tool {"action":"lookup","q":"x"}
assistant: <tool name=lookup>{"id":1,"status":"ok"}</tool>
```
Carla: Two things to check: (1) tokenizer.added_special_tokens vs tokenizer.added_tokens — HF sometimes stores role markers in config.json under different keys; our converter only handled "added_tokens" so role tokens got duplicated/misaligned. (2) sentencepiece merges + special tokenization can split the <tool> tag across token boundaries.
Sam: Also check the JSON-mode sentinel we inject. We currently use "<<JSON>>" (three chars) which collides with some model pre-tokenized sequences. Suggest using a reserved control token ID >= vocab_size or at least add it as an "added_special_token" and force it to be single-token.
DevBot: Conversion CI: hf-to-rw conversion-tests failing (3 tests) — failure class: token-boundary-splits on toolcall tests.
Ben: Quick patch idea: when converter sees a tool tag pattern (<tool.*?>...</tool>), ensure converter registers the open/close tags as added_special_tokens and, if needed, remap to available unused token ids. Example sed to add special tokens in converter manifest: s/"added_tokens"/"added_special_tokens"/ — but we'll do proper JSON edit.
Tina: Note: quantized 4-bit runtime produced different behavior — the split happened after quantization in our internal quantize step. I think quantization script reorders embeddings or pruning that shifted token id lookup for newly added tokens if they were appended incorrectly. Legacy BPE tokenizer saved merges in non-deterministic order in older HF versions; that can change token ids across conversion runs.
Alice: Empirical: after adding explicit added_special_tokens for <tool_open>, <tool_close>, and a dedicated JSON sentinel, toolcall parsing succeeded in 95% cases; failing 5% when running CPU fallback on small batched requests — logs show split at token id boundary: "...<to" + "ol>...". Sample runtime log:
```
[2026-03-18 14:02:11] inference: tokenized len=27 ids=[... 50231, 50232, 12, ...]
[2026-03-18 14:02:11] postproc: joined tokens -> "<to" + "ol>"
```
ML-CI: We should add a roundtrip tokenization test in the eval harness: produce prompt -> tokenize -> detokenize -> assert tool tags intact. Add that to conversion-tests and run across quantization configs (8/4-bit FP). Test name: "token_roundtrip_tool_tags".
Ben: I'll open a small PR on the converter: - detect tool tag regex - add to added_special_tokens array with safe token ids - emit a warning if vocab_size collisions occur. Assigning @Carla for review. I'll also add the roundtrip test to CI.
Carla: sgtm. For long-term, we should change our converter to prefer inserting new tokens into the tokenizer model (hf tokenizer API) rather than naive append in config.json; that avoids id instability across quantize steps.
Alice: Awesome, thanks. I'll run a full eval once the PR lands and report back with regression numbers (latency + failure rate). :thumbsup
